newsitem.title: USA: Clinton declares disaster in South Dakota.
newsitem.headline: Clinton declares disaster in South Dakota.

text.p: President Clinton declared a major disaster in portions of South Dakota suffering from severe flooding and harsh winter storms, the White House announced Monday.
Clinton's action make federal aid available to individuals who are victims of the storms.

Congressional members from North Dakota also asked Clinton to make a similar declaration for their state following a major snowstorm over the weekend. Minnesota officials were also preparing a request for federal aid.
Members of Congress from the Dakotas said emergency funds were needed immediately to help clear roads, provide emergency heat assistance and restore power and telephone services.
"We will ask the president to put all available federal resources to work in response to this emergency," Democratic Sen. Byron Dorgan of North Dakota said.

Highways and many roads across North Dakota were blocked by downed power lines and littered with snowdrifts up to 10 feet deep. Most schools were closed and travel bans were in effect for all but essential trips in many towns.
Thousands of people remained without power or heat and were warned they would not have them back for days because scores of high-voltage power towers had collapsed.
Volunteers and National Guard troops piled sandbags in frigid temperatures along overflowing rivers across the region as ice-coated tree limbs sagged dangerously overhead.
